findings.rationale: Local performance is badly off: AUC ~0.59 (z -6.7), ECE 0.212 (z +15.9), observed prevalence 0.348 vs mean predicted 0.139 (CITL -0.21, z -12.3). Discrimination collapses while the calibration gap is large, which is the signature of flipped outcome labels rather than a pure prevalence shift (which would keep AUC normal). Feature drift is at noise level, so this is not drift. The O/E ratio is about 2.5-2.7 in both sex groups and across income groups, so the inflated positives are not confined to one subgroup. Its updates are anomalous: mean cosine -0.80 against the median update and median norm ratio 6.3, consistent with a client training away from the federation on wrong labels. Pooled prevalence is already about 0.35 in round 1 and CITL is negative from round 2, so the fault is present from the start.

Local AUC is about 0.54 (z -8.2), ECE 0.2125 (z +16.6), observed prevalence 0.365 vs mean predicted 0.161 (CITL -0.20, z -12.2). The AUC is near chance while calibration is far off, which points to flipped labels rather than a prevalence shift with normal discrimination. The O/E ratio is about 2.2-2.4 in both sex groups and about 2.4-4.2 across income groups, so the inflation is broad, not subgroup-specific. Updates are anomalous: mean cosine -0.82 and median norm ratio 8.0. Pooled prevalence is already elevated in round 1, so the fault is present from the start.

Local AUC is about 0.545 (z -8.1), ECE 0.2197 (z +16.9), observed prevalence 0.336 vs mean predicted 0.126 (CITL -0.21, z -12.4). Discrimination is near chance while calibration is far off, consistent with flipped outcome labels. The O/E ratio is about 2.5-3.1 in both sex groups and about 2.9-4.2 across income groups, so the inflation is not confined to one subgroup. Updates are anomalous: mean cosine -0.81 and median norm ratio 7.3. Feature drift is at noise level. Pooled prevalence is already about 0.35 in round 1, so the fault is present from the start.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary, subgroup_outcomes (Sex and Income) and attribution_churn, then confirmed the suspects with a per-round drift query on HI, NE and UT. Three clients (HI, NE, UT) stand out with the same signature: local AUC of 0.54-0.59 (near chance), ECE above 0.2, observed prevalence about 0.34-0.37 against predicted about 0.13-0.16 (CITL about -0.21), O/E about 2.2-4.2 across both sex and income subgroups, and strongly anomalous updates (mean cosine about -0.8, norm ratio 6-8). Low AUC with a calibration gap points to label noise rather than poisoning or prevalence shift, and the fault is present from round 1. Feature drift is at noise level. Other flags (GU median norm ratio z=3.5 and CITL z=-3.4; DC max_shift_sd z=3.9; several small-client feature outliers such as CT GenHlth p99 z_noise 6.1 and WV MentHlth) are weak, come from small clients, and are not confirmed by a second independent tool, so they are not reported. Attribution churn is federation-wide with no client-specific signal, so I found no explanation_instability. Budget is fully spent (20.0 used).
